acts.label: Prologue
acts.desc:
Jackson Landers tells the story of a very strange decision he made one summer day.
The name of today’s show is from a quote by climate futurist Alex Steffen, in an article about wildfires by Elizabeth Weil.
acts.credits: By Ira Glass and Lilly Sullivan

acts.label: Act One
acts.desc:
Elena Kostyuchenko tells the story of how she was probably poisoned after reporting on Russian’s invasion of Ukraine, and how she kept not believing it was happening. Bela Shayevich translated this story from Russian and reads it for us.
We adapted this from an article in n+1 magazine. Elena’s book is I Love Russia: Reporting from a Lost Country.
acts.credits: By Elena Kostyuchenko and Bela Shayevich; Produced by Nancy Updike and Valerie Kipnis
acts.title: It’s Probably Nothing

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc:
A recording of comedian Tig Notaro in the process of trying to catch up to the present and absolutely not being able to.
Tig’s new stand-up special, Hello Again, comes out in two weeks on Amazon. Her podcast, Handsome, is available wherever you get your podcasts.
acts.title: We At The Hotel, Motel, Very Locked In

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc:
Producer Zoe Chace with a political fable that she noticed playing out last week in North Carolina.
Zoe covered Mark Harris’ election fraud case in the podcast The Improvement Association by Serial Productions and The New York Times.
acts.title: That’s My Story and I’m Absolutely Not Sticking to It

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc:
Producer Tobin Low finds a group of people with a special relationship with the idea of catching up.
Visit KLS Foundation for more on Klein-Levine Syndrome.
acts.title: What’d I Miss?
